reasons: The Learn More buttons have no action.
The header count of 12 does not update.
The Filter icon is imported but not used.
The AI-enhanced claims are fixed text.

terms.meaning: A named method for analyzing a business problem, such as SWOT Analysis.
A control that hides items which do not match a chosen category or level.
A reusable part of a screen, here each framework card.
A bar that stays at the top of the screen while the page scrolls.

used_by: The /frameworks address, linked from the home page footer

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the library page
sections.what: Loads React state, the animation library, and icons for each framework and the search and filter controls.
sections.why: Needed for the interactive filters and the icons shown on cards.
sections.watch_out: The Filter icon is imported but never used.

sections.name: Framework
sections.title: Shape of one framework entry
sections.what: Describes each framework: name, summary, category, difficulty, duration, icon, uses, key parts, and whether it is AI-enhanced.
sections.why: Keeps every card the same shape.
sections.watch_out: The icon field accepts any type, so the checker cannot catch a wrong icon.

sections.name: frameworks, categories, difficulties (part 1)
sections.title: First five framework records
sections.what: Records for Porter's Five Forces, BCG Growth-Share Matrix, Ansoff Matrix, McKinsey 7S Framework, and Value Chain Analysis, each with its details.
sections.why: Likely reason: simple static content stored with the page.
sections.watch_out: Content must be edited by hand here, and the header count is separate from this list.

sections.name: frameworks, categories, difficulties (part 2)
sections.title: Next five framework records
sections.what: Records for SWOT Analysis, Jobs-to-be-Done, Lean Canvas, OKR Framework, and Blue Ocean Strategy.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as above, continuing the static list.
sections.watch_out: Every record must keep the same field layout, or the card may fail to show that field.

sections.name: frameworks, categories, difficulties (part 3)
sections.title: Last two records and filter lists
sections.what: Records for Business Model Canvas and Agile Transformation Framework, then the lists of categories and difficulty levels that drive the filter buttons.
sections.why: Gives the filters the exact values they match against.
sections.watch_out: Category names must match exactly between records and the filter list, or a framework disappears from its filter.

sections.name: FrameworksPage (part 1)
sections.title: Search and filter logic with header
sections.what: Keeps three settings in memory: chosen category, chosen difficulty, and search text. A framework shows only if it passes all three checks. The header shows an AI label, a count of 12, and the search box.
sections.why: Lets visitors narrow the list quickly.
sections.watch_out: Search does not look at key parts, so searching for a part name finds nothing.

sections.name: FrameworksPage (part 2)
sections.title: Category and difficulty filter buttons
sections.what: Two rows of buttons. The chosen button is highlighted. Category buttons are blue and difficulty buttons are lime.
sections.why: Gives visitors a visible way to narrow the list.
sections.watch_out: The count of 12 in the header is typed by hand and will not change when filters hide frameworks.

sections.name: FrameworksPage (part 3)
sections.title: Framework card grid and difficulty labels
sections.what: Shows matching frameworks in a two-column grid. Each card has an icon, name, category, colored difficulty label, and an AI badge when enhanced. A message appears when nothing matches.
sections.why: Gives a quick scan of each framework.
sections.watch_out: Any difficulty level not listed in the color rules shows in the advanced blue style.

sections.name: FrameworksPage (part 4)
sections.title: Card details and Learn More button
sections.what: Shows each card's description, uses, up to four key parts with a check mark, a count of any extra parts, the duration, and a Learn More button.
sections.why: Gives enough detail to decide whether to explore a framework.
sections.watch_out: The Learn More button has no action, so visitors clicking it see nothing happen.

sections.name: FrameworksPage (part 5)
sections.title: AI features explainer section
sections.what: A closing section stating all frameworks are AI-enhanced, with three fixed points about data collection, analysis, and human oversight.
sections.why: Likely reason: marketing copy that explains the AI approach.
sections.watch_out: The AI-enhanced claim is repeated as fixed text and per-card flags, so the two can drift apart.

summary: The frameworks library page, where a visitor searches and filters a fixed list of 12 business strategy frameworks shown as cards.
purpose: Lets visitors browse, search, and filter business frameworks such as Porter's Five Forces and SWOT Analysis.
why: Gives visitors one place to see the framework list and narrow it by category, difficulty, or text.
how: The list of frameworks is stored in the file. The page keeps three filter settings in memory. For each framework it checks the category, the difficulty, and the search text, and shows only those that pass all three. Each passing framework is drawn as a card with its details. A closing section describes the AI features.
inputs: Typing in the search box and clicks on category and difficulty buttons.
outputs: A filtered grid of framework cards, or a message saying nothing matches.
risks: The list is hard-coded, so adding a framework means editing this file. The header count is also typed by hand. The Learn More button does nothing. Category names must match exactly.
debug: If a framework is missing from a filter, compare its category with the category list. If search finds nothing, remember it only checks the name, description, and uses. Try resetting both filters to All.
